items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Wynton Marsalis is crazy about him. ... Let's see, Wynton Marsalis, who else —

ctx.x: Well you’re mentioning Gene Ammons reminds me — I wanted to ask you about — for the first part of your career you were playing with different combos and stuff. And eventually you got to a point where you started becoming your own leader, of your trio. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

Yeah. That was years later though after Gene Ammons. I think it was about 1961 that I gave serious thought to becoming a leader. Because I made my first record as a leader in ’58 or ’59, it was a Verve record called “Just Plain Junior.” I was playing with Dizzy at the time. And Norman Granz, who then was the owner of Verve records, was also the producer. So he came out of the booth during the break and said, “How would you like to do your own album?” And I was speechless. I didn’t know what to say. Finally I said…
Yeah. I have that CD you mentioned.
